script.base: WAS@MIA is a one-score outdoor game, not a blowout and not a slog: Miami -2.5, total 47.5, implied team totals MIA 25.0 and WAS 22.5. Miami leads or stays within a score into the fourth and keeps De'Von Achane in the weeks 8-10 role (54 carries, 308 rush yards, 23 targets, 114 receiving yards). Washington is on Marcus Mariota with Jayden Daniels, Terry McLaurin, Treylon Burks and Ben Sinnott out, so the WAS menu stays short: Deebo Samuel 17 targets / 81 yards / 54 air yards and Zach Ertz 15 targets / 116 yards / 155 air yards, with Jacory Croskey-Merritt (32 carries, 93 yards, 2.9 YPC) and Chris Rodriguez (19 carries, 83 yards) splitting a low-efficiency run game. Pace is moderate. Jaylen Waddle remains the Miami downfield piece from that window (22 targets, 265 yards, 325 air yards) unless Tyreek Hill, absent from the weeks 8-10 target log, takes the air yards back.
script.flip1: Miami gets up big early on the ground against a WAS front allowing 4.87 YPC with DE Drake Jackson and LB Ale Kaho out, then runs the clock. Waddle's 75.5 receiving line dies the way favorite-clock games kill WR yards, and WAS abandons the run so Croskey-Merritt (recent rush games 33, 25, 38, 30) and Rodriguez (weeks 8-10 rush 2, 65, 16) fall short. Achane receiving can still clear 23.5 on checkdowns; his rush line 67.5 becomes the clock-kill leg, not the rec line.
